sample_unit: predictions (4,174 true positive and 17,644 false positive)
models_evaluated: logistic regression model predicting high-intensity (top decile) mental health service use

links.outcome: Baseline factors associated with false positive versus true positive predictions, including ethnicity subgroups
links.effect: False positive predictions were more common among Asian service users, those living with family, and users referred by their GP. True positives were associated with voluntary or probation referrals. Numeric estimates not given in the abstract.
links.quote: At baseline, FP predictions were more common among Asian service users, those living with family, and users referred by their GP, whilst TP predictions were associated with voluntary or probation service referrals.

screen.reason: Retrospective error/bias analysis evaluating clinical and demographic factors associated with false positive predictions of an existing high-intensity mental health risk model.
